input.brief: The 26-point gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. District rules send every student below the 40th percentile on the fall test into the program. In September, participants averaged 182.8 and non-participants 215.1, and 91% of participants were below the cut. When the research office compared students with similar fall scores, the gaps shrank to a few points or less, and fall-to-winter growth was about the same in each group. So the dashboard does not show the program hurts students. Northgate's claim of faster growth is also mostly a result of low starters gaining more, so it does not show the program works. The current data cannot detect a small effect either way. Don't end the contract or expand it yet, and don't open sign-up to everyone. That would undo the targeting and make future comparisons harder. Ending the contract would also leave the district without its designated intervention, which the state rule requires. Next steps: have the research office present the matched comparison instead of the raw chart, and ask for the comparison of students just above and just below the cut (ready 27 Feb).
